newsitem.title: USA: Brent climbs in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: Brent climbs in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: Bellwether North Sea Brent crude climbed in late U.S. paper trading Friday, with a top Wall Street player attributed with most of the buying, traders said.
A series of partial paper March Brents changed hands a total of 600 times between $22.57 and $22.65 a barrel, traders said.
London's IPE closed at $22.52 a barrel.
March/April Brent moved twice at 48 and 47.5 cents a barrel, up about one cent from the London close.

Meanwhile, the spread between Brent and U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing continued a gradual narrowing trend at around $1.60-65 a barrel, down five cents from Thursday and 10 cents from Wednesday, traders said.

Although the transatlantic arbitrage is still open, traders said the price for Brent deliveries into the U.S. Gulf Coast has climbed to around WTI minus 10 cents a barrel, making domestic grades such as Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James --Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
